thread.title: Apple: The Watch Helps It Keep the Q1 Wearables Lead

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Apple: The Watch Helps It Keep the Q1 Wearables Lead
text:
Photo: Justin Sullivan/Getty 9:55 a.m. ET Apple maintained its lead in global wearables shipments in the first quarter as the Apple Watch, driven by wider availability of cellular connectivity, according to new estimates.
Xiaomi and Fitbit (FIT) rounded out the top three, maintaining their positions from 2017 , while Huawei and Garmin (GRMN) rounded out the top five, according to IDC.
 Global wearables shipments rose 1.2% to just over 25 million, IDC wrote, slowing substantially from a year ago as basic wearables lost steam. About a third of all wearables included cellular connectivity in Q1, IDC wrote.
Watches and wristbands accounted for 95% of all shipments, with clothing that includes sensors—mainly, in Q1, shoes with step counters—seeing growth of nearly 60%.
“While health and fitness remain the key value proposition behind many of these devices, a closer look reveals wearables that feature coaching, audio modification, and language translation, other wrist-worn devices focusing on personal safety, and connected watches for children,” IDC analyst Ramon Llamas wrote in a release.
Illustration: IDC Smartwatch sales could top 70 million this year, and then double by 2022, according to some estimates .
Barron’s Next 50 company Apple (AAPL) shipments rose 13.5% from last year’s Q1 to 4 million, according to IDC, while Xiaomi’s ticked up slightly to 3.7 million. Fitbit’s fell more than 28% to 2.2 million.
Newsletter Sign-up Fossil (FOSL), which was fifth globally in 2017 shipments according to IDC, didn’t make the top 5 in Q1. In a Monday note, KeyBanc analysts raised their price target on the company’s shares to $32, citing pleasure with the company’s current products.
“The company is well-positioned to be the number-two player in wearables,” the analysts wrote.
